events.artist: Gabriel Cabezas / Natalia Kazaryan / Domenic Salerni
events.subtitle: Obliquely Wrecked — The piano trio, rewired
events.category: Contemporary piano trio / extended-technique chamber music
events.factual_description: Counterpoint Concerts presents Obliquely Wrecked at The Powerhouse in Washington, DC on Friday, November 6, 2026. Doors and bar open at 6:30 PM and the performance begins at 7:00 PM. The announced trio is Gabriel Cabezas on cello, Natalia Kazaryan on piano, and Domenic Salerni on violin. The complete published program is Katherine Balch's different gravities, Shawn Okpebholo's City Beautiful, Pascal Le Boeuf's Obliquely Wrecked, and Maurice Ravel's Piano Trio in A minor, M. 67. Counterpoint describes the three living-composer works as exploring prepared and extended techniques, unconventional timbres and experimental or industrial-inflected sound worlds before the Ravel closes the program. Face-value admission is listed at $45. The exact official ticket page currently says the event is sold out and offers a waitlist if inventory returns.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is the form itself: the same piano-trio body moves through three living composers who treat preparation, extended technique and timbre as structural material, then lands on Ravel's A-minor trio. That sequence lets the ear hear how far violin, cello and piano can be bent before the familiar chamber architecture snaps back into focus.
en.trip_verdict: For a DC night, this is worth catching if the waitlist opens and the evening is free. I would not reorganize the regional calendar around it, but the program is distinctive enough that a returned ticket would be an easy yes.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho está en la forma misma: el mismo cuerpo de trío con piano pasa por tres compositores vivos que usan preparación, técnicas extendidas y timbre como material estructural, y después aterriza en el trío en la menor de Ravel. Esa secuencia permite oír hasta dónde se pueden doblar violín, cello y piano antes de que vuelva a aparecer con claridad la arquitectura camerística conocida.
es.trip_verdict: Para una noche en DC, sí entraría si se abre la lista de espera y la fecha está libre. No reorganizaría el calendario regional por este concierto, pero el programa es suficientemente particular como para agarrar sin pensarlo demasiado un boleto que reaparezca.

events.artist: Natalia Kazaryan / Eric Lee (easterner) / Gen Tomuro / Toru Izumida
events.subtitle: Tokyo Tunnel — Ondine rises in Tokyo
events.category: Tokyo–US audiovisual chamber collaboration / Ravel reimagining
events.factual_description: Counterpoint Concerts presents Tokyo Tunnel at Tunnel Tokyo in Shinagawa on Saturday, November 28, 2026. The freshest current presenter-page crawl lists doors at 4:30 PM and the performance from 5:00 PM to 6:30 PM. Natalia Kazaryan performs Ravel's Gaspard de la nuit in a live audiovisual collaboration with New York-based artist Eric Lee, also known as easterner, using real-time generative visuals. Tokyo-based pianist Gen Tomuro and audio/visual artist Toru Izumida extend the program with solo piano and audiovisual sets. The published program includes Ravel's Jeux d'eau, an easterner electronic audiovisual interlude, the complete three movements of Gaspard de la nuit (Ondine, Le gibet, Scarbo), and a closing electronic audiovisual set. Counterpoint frames the event as a new international edition of its earlier Guardian of the Night project. The presenter lists a $35 ticket option and says Japanese and international-card ticketing is available via Teket. Counterpoint's older shop copy currently shows a stale 7:30 PM time and a Friday label for November 28; those older time/day fields are not used here because November 28, 2026 is Saturday and the fresher event page supplies the current 4:30 PM doors / 5:00 PM performance schedule.

en.why_it_matters: This is a genuine Tokyo–US exchange built into the performance rather than pasted onto the billing: Kazaryan's Ravel is re-engineered through Eric Lee's live generative visuals, then Tokyo-based Gen Tomuro and Toru Izumida answer with their own piano and audiovisual sets. Gaspard de la nuit is already about image, menace and illusion; putting its three movements inside a live visual system gives the work a new physical architecture without turning it into background music for projections.
en.trip_verdict: If November 28 is part of a Tokyo stay, actively make room for Shinagawa and let this anchor the late afternoon. I would not build a Japan trip around this one performance alone, but inside Tokyo it is exactly the kind of cross-cultural, instrument-plus-technology night worth protecting from routine itinerary drift.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí el intercambio Tokio–Estados Unidos está metido dentro de la función y no pegado al cartel: el Ravel de Kazaryan se rehace con las visuales generativas en tiempo real de Eric Lee, y después los artistas de Tokio Gen Tomuro y Toru Izumida responden con sus propios sets de piano y audiovisual. Gaspard de la nuit ya vive de imagen, amenaza e ilusión; poner sus tres movimientos dentro de un sistema visual en vivo le da una arquitectura física nueva sin reducir la música a acompañamiento de proyecciones.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 28 de noviembre cae dentro de una estancia en Tokio, sí le haría espacio activamente a Shinagawa y dejaría que esta función ancle la tarde. No construiría un viaje a Japón únicamente alrededor de ella, pero ya estando en Tokio es exactamente el tipo de noche entre instrumento, tecnología e intercambio cultural que conviene proteger del itinerario rutinario.
